doctrine: A board claim is never truth on its own. The evidence field carries the proof. The executor updates this JSON at every checkpoint and re-renders. A card may not enter status=shipped with evidence=null; a launch gate condition may not be state=pass with evidence=null. Enforced by docs/board/validate-board.mjs. GATE VOCABULARY on this project: green_self_merge = an executor terminal merges its own PR once the required checks are green (routine code and docs). ivan_merge = Ivan clears the merge - anything touching production data, money, credentials, security boundaries, or visual work he reviews on a deployed screen. adam_authorizes = the owner authorises before anything is built or spent - product decisions, paid-tier upgrades, account ownership changes. stakeholder = an outside party signs off (Shopify app review, a payment processor, counsel); reserved, no card carries it yet. MERGE AUTHORITY, granted by Ivan 2026-08-20 once branch protection went live on main (PRs mandatory, required checks typecheck + lint + build, no bypass): a green_self_merge card is merged by the executor terminal itself once ALL required checks are green, squash merge, branch deleted after. ivan_merge, adam_authorizes and stakeholder are unchanged and are never merged by an executor. If a card's gate field contradicts a verbal grant, THE BOARD JSON WINS: halt on that card and flag it. MERGING IS NOT SHIPPING. Non-visual work (SEC, CODE, INFRA, CHORE) ships on merge with the PR as evidence. Any UI or visual card ships only on Ivan's deployed-screen confirmation, whoever merged it, because a green check proves the code compiles, lints and builds and cannot prove a screen looks right. RED IS NEVER MERGED: a check that flakes or reddens is fixed or halted on, and disabling, relaxing or narrowing a check to obtain green is forbidden. See BOARD-SPEC.md, Merge authority. HOME_LANE IS A KIND, NOT AN ACTIVITY CLAIM: a card sits in in_flight because it is a work item on the active queue, and its status says whether anyone is executing it. Card census moves; read it from the validator output rather than from this sentence. DESIGN VERSUS CODE, set by Ivan 2026-08-20 with the W1 dispatch: when a design and the code disagree about FACTS (limits, counts, categories, quotas, prices) the CODE is the truth and the COPY is changed to tell the truth. When they disagree about INTENT (features, flows, whole screens) it becomes a card gated adam_authorizes. Design wins on VISUALS only. Never ship copy that promises what the code rejects. Copy that states a limit should read from the constant that enforces it, so a later ruling changes one value rather than a value and a sentence that drift apart. See BOARD-SPEC.md, Design versus code.

cards.title: /login submit returned the raw Supabase gateway error "Invalid path specified in request URL"; root cause was a malformed NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, corrected by Ivan

evidence.ref: Ivan confirmed on deployed instance 2026-08-20, both logins green after env correction

cards.notes: Reported by Ivan 2026-08-20 against https://lablld-1.vercel.app: submitting /login showed "Invalid path specified in request URL". RESOLVED by an env correction on Ivan's side; he confirmed on the deployed instance that both an admin and a merchant account now log in cleanly. MECHANISM, re-derived from the installed code rather than transcribed: supabase-js 2.99.1 builds every sub-API URL by RELATIVE resolution against the env value (dist/index.mjs:367-398, new URL('auth/v1', ensureTrailingSlash(NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL))). Any path segment left in that variable is therefore preserved, the auth request lands on a route the Supabase gateway does not serve, and the gateway answers with exactly that string. The message reached the user's screen in English because translateAuthError (app/(auth)/actions.ts) had no branch for it and returned the upstream text unchanged. That display defect is fixed in the same PR that carries this card. REQUIRED SHAPE, variable name only: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL must be scheme plus host and nothing else - no path, no /rest/v1 or /auth/v1 suffix, no dashboard URL. No secret value was read, requested, printed or logged at any point in this incident.

cards.title: /register crashed with "Application error: a client-side exception has occurred"; cleared by the same NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL correction, throw site never captured

evidence.ref: Ivan confirmed on deployed instance 2026-08-20, both logins green after env correction

cards.notes: Reported by Ivan 2026-08-20: /register threw "Application error: a client-side exception has occurred", a full crash rather than the intentional signup gating Adam described. The gating itself is configured in Supabase Auth and is NOT a defect; the crash was. RESOLVED: Ivan confirmed on the deployed instance that /register no longer crashes after the same NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL correction that cleared INC-01. The card closes on that confirmation. THE THROW SITE WAS NEVER CAPTURED AND IS RECORDED HERE AS UNPROVEN. The reported mechanism - the malformed URL throwing at the client factory's URL scheme check before network I/O - was tested locally against the installed @supabase/supabase-js 2.99.1 and @supabase/ssr 0.9.0 and is FALSIFIED, two independent ways. (1) @supabase/ssr delegates to the same supabase-js createClient (ssr/dist/main/createServerClient.js:16), so the URL shapes that DO throw at the scheme check - no scheme, empty, undefined - throw identically in all three factories. proxy.ts:8 constructs a client from that same variable on every matched request, and the matcher covers both /login and /register, so such a value would have failed at the edge and neither page would have rendered at all. (2) The only URL shape that produces INC-01's gateway response is a path-suffixed URL, and that shape was probed and constructs CLEANLY in all three factories; it never throws. One env value cannot both throw at the factory and reach the gateway. Since /login rendered and displayed a gateway message, the URL parsed. WHAT IS CERTAIN: the env correction cleared it, and this app has no error.tsx and no global-error.tsx anywhere in app/, so ANY uncaught throw renders that exact default message and names no location. WHAT IS NOT KNOWN: which statement threw. No server stack trace was taken, Vercel runtime log access is permanently off limits by Ivan's ruling of 2026-08-20, and the defect no longer reproduces. Do not build on the reported mechanism. MITIGATION SHIPPED WITH THIS CARD: the three auth entry points now reach the Supabase factories through lib/supabase/safe.ts and fail CLOSED with a Spanish message instead of throwing, and registerAction no longer discards the error from its merchants pre-check - a discarded error there read as "this email is free" and let registration proceed on an unknown answer. ACCEPTED TRADEOFF, stated rather than buried: the fix adds NO logging, because CLAUDE.md forbids console output and the repo holds that rule perfectly (zero console.* calls in app/, lib/, components/ and proxy.ts). A configuration failure is therefore now silent to the operator: the user sees a readable message and the app stays up, but nothing records why. Introducing a logging convention inside an incident hotfix was the wrong place to decide it. That gap belongs to INFRA-billing-alerting, which already owns "no error reporting anywhere in the codebase", and is noted on it. See also CODE-error-boundaries, the card that would have made this incident legible instead of anonymous.

cards.title: Add HMAC verification to /api/shopify/fulfillment_order_notification; it is an unauthenticated, unsigned service-role write path while its five sibling webhooks all verify
cards.notes: P0 · Source: docs/audit/CODE-AUDIT-2026-08.md R3. Launch gate G5 does not pass until this is closed. WORKED 2026-08-20 by PINK, PR #2, awaiting Ivan's merge (ivan_merge gate), so it is in_flight and not shipped: it flips to shipped with a pr evidence ref on merge. RE-DERIVED FROM CODE, AND THE CARD'S FRAMING IS INCOMPLETE. This is not one unsigned endpoint among five signed siblings. TWO routes handle this event, both registered on every OAuth connect, both performing the identical service-role write on orders: /api/shopify/fulfillment_order_notification, reached because registerFulfillmentService sets callback_url to {WEBHOOK_URL}/api/shopify (lib/shopify.ts:101) and Shopify appends the notification path; and /api/webhooks/shopify/fulfillment-order, registered for topic fulfillment_orders/fulfillment_request_submitted (app/api/shopify/callback/route.ts:55-59). Only the second verified. The second also carried its own INLINE dual-secret verifier, because the two registration paths are signed with different secrets: a programmatic topic webhook with SHOPIFY_API_SECRET, a Dev Dashboard registration with its own SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET. FIX: that verifier is exported from lib/shopify.ts as verifyFulfillmentHmac and both routes now use it, so the boundary has one implementation instead of one implementation and one hole. NEITHER ROUTE DELETED: which of the two Shopify actually delivers to is a live-system fact and no LABLLD terminal has production access. Verifying both breaks nothing; deleting the wrong one silently breaks fulfillment tracking. PROVEN at authoring time against the real exported function, 6 cases green (valid under either secret accepts; attacker secret, absent header, short header, and a valid signature for a different body all reject) plus a NEGATIVE ARM: with the guard removed the forged request is accepted, which is what makes those assertions load-bearing. The probe becomes a committed test in INFRA-ci-and-tests, card 4 of this wave. OPEN RISK FOR IVAN: if Shopify's fulfillment-service callback carries no X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 header, this endpoint now 401s where it used to accept. Unverifiable from code. Mitigating fact: the signed sibling receives the same event and does the same write, so the column still gets populated; the failure mode is a redundant path going quiet, not lost data. Confirm after merge by connecting a store, placing a test order, and checking orders.shopify_fulfillment_order_id. Merged 2026-08-20 by Ivan (ivan_merge). Non-visual, so it ships on merge with the PR as evidence, per the merge-authority grant of the same day. STILL OPEN AND NOT A BLOCKER TO SHIPPING: whether Shopify's fulfillment-service callback carries an X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 header is unverifiable from code, and if it does not this endpoint now 401s where it used to accept. The signed sibling receives the same event and performs the identical write, so the failure mode is a redundant path going quiet, not lost data. Confirm by connecting a store, placing a test order, and checking orders.shopify_fulfillment_order_id.

cards.notes: P1 · Source: audit §5 privacy finding; docs/db/SCHEMA-RECONSTRUCTION-NOTES.md C11; ruling 2026-08-20 (public authored for parity only, exposure not accepted). Launch gate G5 does not pass until this is closed. WORKED 2026-08-20 by PINK, code PR #9. in_flight, and it stays in_flight through the migration apply: per Ivan's sequencing the code ships first, he applies the bucket flip in the dashboard, he confirms labels still render on the deployed instance, and only then does this card ship. WHY THAT ORDER: a private bucket with getPublicUrl() still live returns 403 for every label, so labels would silently stop rendering for merchants and for admins working the approval queue. The deployed code signs every read AND falls back to the stored public URL when signing fails, so it is correct against a public bucket and a private one. That fallback is what makes the order safe rather than merely preferred. MIGRATION AUTHORED, NOT APPLIED: supabase/migrations/0003_labels_bucket_private.sql. It flips storage.buckets.public to false for labels and replaces the labels_read_all policy (which was `to public`, mirroring the bucket flag) with an owner-or-admin read. product-images is deliberately untouched. Ivan applies it in the dashboard; no LABLLD terminal touches a database. THE DESIGN DECISION THAT DEVIATES FROM THE CARD SCOPE, and the reason: the scope said migrate BOTH UPLOADERS to createSignedUrl. The uploaders were deliberately left alone, because label_url is an IDENTITY as well as a locator. Three sites match on its exact value: app/api/admin/labels/[id]/route.ts:56 does .eq('label_url', label.label_url) to approve or reject, app/admin/labels/page.tsx:46-48 keys a map on merchant_id:label_url, and components/merchant/label-picker.tsx:32 compares equality. Storing a signed, expiring URL would break label APPROVAL silently: the .eq() would match zero rows. Worse, product-stepper.tsx:32 seeds its state from label_url and saves it back through saveMerchantProductAction, so a signed URL would be PERSISTED into the database and expire there. The stored value therefore stays the canonical public form and signing happens at render only. If Ivan wants the stored form changed it is a data migration and a separate card. SIGNED AT: app/(merchant)/labels/page.tsx, app/admin/labels/page.tsx, app/admin/orders/[id]/page.tsx (the order-detail thumbnails), and app/(merchant)/orders/page.tsx which feeds the client order panel. PLUS ONE NOT IN THE CARD SCOPE AND EASY TO MISS: app/(merchant)/products/[id]/actions.ts hands label_url to SudoMock, which fetches it from OUTSIDE our network. A private bucket 403s the stored public form, so mockup generation would have broken. It is now signed with a shorter 10-minute TTL because that URL leaves our control. THREE no-img-element DEFERRALS FROM PR #5 RESOLVED, and one of them was resolved by correcting my own earlier reasoning. app/admin/orders/[id]/page.tsx and components/merchant/order-tab-panel.tsx now carry a permanent decision instead of a deferral: the src is a signed, expiring URL, so every render is a fresh optimizer cache miss and a fresh billable transformation, which makes next/image the wrong tool. The THIRD, components/merchant/product-step-label.tsx, was never a labels URL at all. It renders theme previews from the PUBLIC product-images bucket (theme-labels-editor.tsx:36 uploads there), so the reason I wrote in PR #5 was simply wrong. The comment now says so and hands it to the UI wave as an ordinary decision. The two existing next/image label usages gained `unoptimized` for the same cost reason, and because a signed URL's path is /storage/v1/object/sign/... which does not match the /storage/v1/object/public/** remotePattern in next.config.ts and would have 400d in the optimizer. SEEDED OR MOCK LABEL OBJECTS: NONE, confirmed from code paths as instructed. supabase/seed.sql contains zero references to merchant_products or merchant_labels; it inserts admin_emails and three products only. Nothing to migrate. DEAD CODE LEFT ALONE: components/merchant/label-picker.tsx, product-configure-form.tsx and product-label-panel.tsx all read label_url but are UNREACHABLE (product-configure-form has no parent and is LabelPicker's only importer). They are CODE-delete-dead-files' problem; polishing dead code would have widened this diff for no behaviour. PROVEN: labelObjectPath exercised directly, 6 cases, including the negative arm that a product-images URL returns null so the wrong bucket can never be signed. tsc, eslint --max-warnings=0 and a full next build all green locally. SHIPPED 2026-08-20. Ivan applied 0003 in the dashboard and confirmed on the deployed instance: labels bucket shows Private, product-images still Public, /labels renders clean and /admin/labels renders clean. WHAT WAS NOT PROVEN, recorded because the surfaces were empty and a clean render of an empty page proves less than it looks like it does: both label pages rendered their EMPTY STATE, because no label data exists yet, and the admin order-detail thumbnail was NOT TESTABLE because zero orders exist. So the bucket is private and nothing errors, but the signed-URL happy path (upload -> store -> sign -> render) has never executed end to end. The first real label upload is what proves it. That note is carried on UI-product-create-flow, the W1 card whose stepper contains the label upload step. RULINGS CONFIRMED BY IVAN AND NOW DOCTRINE: label_url stays canonical with sign-at-render; the SudoMock 10-minute TTL is approved; the next/image deferrals on signed surfaces are permanent, not deferred.

cards.title: OAuth state is generated at app/api/shopify/auth/route.ts:23 and never verified; the callback reads it and discards it, so CSRF protection on the handshake is decorative (Shopify HMAC still applies)
cards.notes: P2 · Source: audit §8.5(b). ADDED-BY-SWEEP. WORKED 2026-08-20 by PINK, PR #8. in_flight, not shipped: the gate is ivan_merge and the board JSON wins over the self-merge grant, so this one waits for Ivan. Last of the six W0 cards. CARD CONFIRMED EXACTLY: state was generated with crypto.randomBytes(16) at app/api/shopify/auth/route.ts:23 and stored nowhere, so the callback had nothing to compare against. FIX: the auth route persists the state in an HttpOnly cookie and the callback compares in constant time, 403 on mismatch. The cookie name and the compare live in lib/shopify.ts so the two routes cannot drift. FOUR DELIBERATE DETAILS, recorded because each is a place where the obvious choice is wrong. SameSite=Lax not Strict: the callback is a cross-site top-level navigation from Shopify and Strict would withhold the cookie and break every install, so Strict is the more secure-LOOKING setting and the broken one. State is checked AFTER the HMAC check: HMAC proves Shopify sent it, state proves this browser started it, and the cheaper stronger one runs first. A FAILED CHECK DOES NOT CLEAR THE COOKIE: clearing on failure would let anyone break a real merchant's pending install by hitting the callback URL with a wrong state. It is single-use on every path PAST the check and expires on its own in ten minutes. Length is compared before timingSafeEqual because the caller controls the query parameter and timingSafeEqual throws on a length mismatch. PROVEN against the real exported function, 7 cases: genuine round trip accepts; attacker state, absent state, absent cookie, both absent, wrong length and a single changed character all reject. NEGATIVE ARM: with the guard removed the forged callback is accepted. SCOPE NOTE: the card says Shopify HMAC still applies, and that stays true. This was never an open door; the missing leg was the binding to the browser that started the flow. ALSO REMOVES the eslint-disable added in PR #5 for the unused state read. That marker existed to keep the hole visible; the hole is closed, so it goes. NEEDS A DEPLOYED CHECK, the one thing a unit probe cannot prove: connect a store from /settings/shopify end to end after merge. A 403 Invalid state means the cookie is not surviving the round trip. SHIPPED: merged by Ivan 2026-08-20 (ivan_merge). Non-visual, so it ships on merge with the PR as evidence. Flipped late, in PR #9 rather than at merge time, because I did not re-check the board after Ivan reported the merge. The runtime proof it still lacks is tracked on VERIFY-shopify-e2e, deferred behind G4 by Ivan's ruling of the same day, not held open here.

cards.title: No error.tsx and no global-error.tsx anywhere in app/, so every uncaught throw renders Next's default white page naming neither cause nor location; INC-02 was undiagnosable for this reason
cards.notes: Discovered while diagnosing INC-02 and recorded rather than fixed, because it is user-visible surface and belongs to Ivan's deployed-screen review, not to an incident hotfix. find app -name error.tsx -o -name global-error.tsx returns nothing. Consequence: any throw in a Server Component, a route handler or a Server Action reaches the browser as "Application error: a client-side exception has occurred" with no digest surfaced to the operator and no recovery affordance for the user. Scope when built: a root app/error.tsx and app/global-error.tsx in the LABLLD visual system, both surfacing the Next error digest so a production failure can be correlated without log access, plus a decision on whether the merchant and admin segments want their own boundaries. Depends on the visual system, so sequence it with the UI wave, not before. W1 CARD ZERO, worked 2026-08-20 by PINK, PR #11. Ships on merge per Ivan's dispatch; his screen check rides along with the first UI card. BUILT: app/error.tsx and app/global-error.tsx, Spanish, branded, each with a reset action, and both surfacing error.digest, which is the only handle an operator gets on a production failure and the thing whose absence made INC-02 undiagnosable. global-error.tsx replaces the ROOT layout, so it renders its own html and body with inline styles and depends on neither Manrope nor globals.css, because the moment it fires is exactly when a font or stylesheet may be the thing that failed. PROVEN, not assumed, and the proof found two things worth recording. A temporary throwing route was built and served in PRODUCTION mode. First: the SSR HTML contains only an error marker (5:E with a digest) and NOT the boundary UI, because Next 16 renders the boundary on the client after hydration, so curl can never verify this and a browser check is mandatory. Second: loaded in a real browser it rendered 'Algo salio mal.', both actions, and 'Codigo del error: 4226927970' matching the digest in the server log exactly, which proves the correlation handle works end to end. The browser check also caught a defect no compiler would: min-h-[60vh] left the lower viewport white, because this boundary always renders STANDALONE (there is no nested error.tsx, so it replaces the merchant and admin chrome too). Changed to min-h-screen. The probe route was deleted; the tree is clean.
